name: Solomon
overview: Solomon was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely known as the son of David. He is recognized as a significant biblical figure, particularly noted for his role in Israel's monarchy and his lineage as David's son. No additional personal notes are provided beyond these foundational details.
namesAndTitles: The name Solomon means 'peace, well-being,' reflecting a sense of tranquility associated with his identity. He was also called Jedidiah, meaning 'beloved of YHWH,' highlighting a divine favor. His titles include King Solomon and King of Israel, emphasizing his royal status, and Preacher, denoting his role as a teacher and instructor of the assembly.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Solomon as the son of David and Bathsheba. He was also the father of Rehoboam and had familial ties through marriage to Pharaoh, his son-in-law. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Taphath and Basemath, indicating a notable family lineage connected to the royal house.
scriptureSignificance: Solomon holds a pivotal place in the biblical narrative as Israel's third king, endowed with exceptional wisdom from God. He is credited with constructing the temple in Jerusalem, a central place of worship pointing forward to Christ as the true temple. Solomon's writings, including Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Solomon, contribute profoundly to biblical wisdom literature. Despite his God-given wisdom, his later years were marked by idolatry influenced by his many foreign wives, which ultimately led to the division of the kingdom after his reign.
